title: The tools, read whole (Rule of Benedict 4)
hook: the full list of seventy-some tools of good works
tomorrow: how much should God be loved? who would dare name an amount?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Breastplate: Christ before, behind, beneath and above, and in every eye that sees me. The line was christ with me.

Losing a borrowed tool on your first day has its own sinking feeling. Gregory the Great tells of a Goth, a newcomer at Benedict's monastery, handed a hooked blade to clear brambles beside a lake. He swings hard, the iron flies off the handle, and it sinks out of sight. He's left holding a stick, and he runs to own up, shaking. In Benedict's house, tools mattered. So what does the abbot do?
screen: `A BORROWED BLADE, LOST.` → `HE RUNS TO OWN UP.` → `WHAT DOES THE ABBOT DO?`

segments.voice: Benedict takes the handle, holds it in the water, and the blade comes back up onto it. He hands it over with a few words: here, work, and don't be sad. No lecture. The tool goes back into the newcomer's hands. That's the spirit of chapter four of Benedict's Rule, where he hangs a whole wall of what he calls the tools of good works. First, the big two. Love the Lord God with all your heart, all your soul, all your strength, and your neighbor as yourself. Second, the hands. Relieve the poor, clothe the naked, visit the sick, bury the dead, console the grieving. Right beside them: prefer nothing to the love of Christ. Third, the heart and the tongue. Don't act on anger, don't nurse a grudge, pray for your enemies, make peace with someone before the sun goes down. Fourth, the last tool and the workshop. The list ends: never despair of God's mercy. Then Benedict says where the tools get used. The workshop is the enclosure of the monastery and stability in the community: staying put with the same people. Tools get dropped there, like the Goth's blade. The Rule's answer is the abbot's: pick it up, and back to work.
screen: `WORK, AND DON'T BE SAD.` · `LOVE GOD, LOVE NEIGHBOR.` · `MAKE PEACE BEFORE SUNSET.` · `NEVER DESPAIR OF GOD'S MERCY.` · then, large: `TOOLS FOR THE WORKSHOP.`

segments.voice: If you have the Rule of Benedict nearby, or on your phone, open chapter four and read it straight through, slowly, without stopping to grade yourself. If not, hold four tools from today: love, help, make peace, never despair. Notice which one your hands reach for first.
The tools. Benedict's wall of good works, used in one workshop: a community you stay with.
Pocket this one: tools for the workshop, dropped sometimes and handed back. See you tomorrow.

notes: Paraphrased from RB 4 (Verheyen's translation is widely shared but not on the public-domain list here). Confirm each tool named: love God with whole heart, soul and strength; neighbor as self; relieve the poor, clothe the naked, visit the sick, bury the dead, console the sorrowing; prefer nothing to the love of Christ; not to act on anger or nurse a grudge; pray for enemies; make peace before sunset; never despair of God's mercy; the closing lines on the tools of the spiritual craft and the workshop (the enclosure of the monastery and stability in the community).

Gregory, Dialogues 2.6, paraphrased: a Goth received into the community clears brambles by the lake with a billhook; the iron flies off into the water; he confesses it trembling (to Maurus, in the story, who tells Benedict); Benedict holds the handle in the water, the iron returns to it, and he gives it back saying 'work, and be sad no more'.
